content.text: I'll act as the Safe Healing Agent for this PR. Let me start by loading the best-practices skill and fetching the PR comments.

# Skill: Safe Healing Agent Best Practices

This document outlines the standard methodologies and best practices for using an AI Safe Healing Agent. The purpose of this agent is to take an MR/PR link, read the review comments left by human reviewers or other AI agents, and autonomously apply the requested fixes.

## 🤖 AI Agent - Execution Modes
When this skill is loaded by an AI Agent (like Claude Code), the Agent MUST determine the execution environment:
- **CI / Non-Interactive Mode (e.g., Jenkins)**: DO NOT ask any clarifying questions to the user. Automatically proceed with fetching comments, checking out the code, applying the fixes, and pushing the changes. If an error occurs, print a detailed log and exit.
- **Interactive Mode (Local CLI)**: Present the user with the following interactive option:
  - **Heal a PR/MR based on review comments** using `/safe-heal <url>`

### Command Definition:
- `/safe-heal <url>`: 
  1. The agent will use the GitHub CLI (e.g., `gh pr view <url> --comments`) or GitLab CLI to fetch the latest code review comments and feedback.
  2. **Complexity Routing**: The agent MUST extract the routing result (e.g., `ROUTING=COMPLEX` or `ROUTING=SIMPLE`) directly from the PR comments generated by the previous MR review. If `COMPLEX`, the agent MUST use a high-capacity model (e.g., Claude 3.5 Sonnet) for the healing process. If `SIMPLE`, use a fast/cheap model (e.g., Claude 3 Haiku).
  3. The agent will check out the PR's branch locally (e.g., `gh pr checkout <url>`).
  4. The agent will read the relevant source files mentioned in the comments.
  5. The agent will safely apply the exact code changes requested in the review.
  6. The agent will automatically **commit and push** the fixes back to the PR's remote branch.
  7. The agent will optionally reply to the PR stating that the issues have been resolved.

## Core Principles of Safe Healing
1. **Address All Feedback**: Ensure that every unresolved comment in the PR is accounted for. Do not leave requested changes hanging.
2. **Minimal Changes**: Only modify the code necessary to address the reviewer's comment. Do not perform unrelated refactoring.
3. **Context Awareness**: If a comment asks for a change that violates SOLID principles, causes a compilation error, or breaks a test, the agent must alert the user rather than blindly applying a breaking change.
4. **Auto-Commit**: The agent should always commit its fixes using a descriptive message like `fix: addressed PR review comments`.

## Prompt Template
If you are calling this manually without the slash command, you can use the prompt located at:
*👉 [prompts/safe-healing-prompt.md](../../prompts/safe-healing-prompt.md)*

*Automated MR review — Senior Frontend/UI-Automation lens. Project detected as a **Playwright UI test-automation framework** (reviewed with FE guidelines). Routing determined by `mr-complexity-analyzer.sh`: `pom.xml` is a core build file → **COMPLEX**.*

---

### 0. 🧭 Complexity Routing
`ROUTING=COMPLEX` — REASON: Core/Config file modified (`pom.xml`). STATS: Files=1, Lines=+27 -0.

### 1. 🚨 Critical Issues
- **Coverage metric is misleading for this project type.** JaCoCo instruments *this project's own bytecode* and reports coverage of the framework/page-object/test classes — **not** the application under test (saucedemo.com, an external web app). For an E2E UI-automation repo there is no meaningful "application coverage" to capture here; the resulting `%` measures how much of your own helper code the tests exercise, which can be mistaken by stakeholders for product coverage. The business value of this plugin in this repo should be justified in the PR description before merge.

### 2. ⚠️ Warnings & Improvements
- **`report` is bound to `verify`, but E2E suites are typically run with `mvn test`.** With this binding, `mvn test` (the common invocation for a Playwright/JUnit suite) will run the JaCoCo agent and produce `target/jacoco.exec` but will **never generate the HTML/XML report**, since `report` only fires at `verify`. CI/dev must explicitly run `mvn verify` or the report silently won't appear. Consider documenting the required goal, or binding `report` to a phase that runs during `test`.
- **`prepare-agent` relies on Surefire's default `argLine` propagation.** JaCoCo injects the agent via the `argLine` property. The existing Surefire config (`forkCount=1`, `reuseForks=true`) does not set `<argLine>` today, so it works — but this is fragile. If anyone later adds an explicit `<argLine>` to Surefire (e.g. for JVM opts / `-Dplaywright...`) without using `@{argLine}` or `${argLine}`, the agent will be dropped and coverage will silently read 0%. Worth a comment near the Surefire config warning future maintainers.
- **No coverage `check` / thresholds.** The report is purely informational and cannot fail the build. If the intent is to *enforce* coverage, a `check` execution with `<rules>` is needed; otherwise the metric will drift unnoticed.

### 3. 💬 Suggestions
- Add `target/jacoco.exec` and the generated report directory to `.gitignore` if not already covered, to avoid accidentally committing build artifacts.
- Pin the report `outputDirectory`/formats explicitly (XML for CI ingestion, e.g. Sonar/Codecov) if downstream tooling will consume it — the default HTML-only report isn't machine-consumable.
- Consider whether coverage belongs in a dedicated Maven **profile** (e.g. `-Pcoverage`) so the agent overhead isn't added to every normal test run.
- The `<jacoco.version>0.8.12</jacoco.version>` property and plugin are clean and pinned — good. Add a one-line note in the README on how to generate/read the report (`mvn verify`, then open `target/site/jacoco/index.html`).

--

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.saucedemo</groupId>
    <artifactId>saucedemo-ui-playwright</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>saucedemo-ui-playwright</name>
    <description>E2E UI automation for Swag Labs (saucedemo.com) using Playwright + JUnit 5</description>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>

        <playwright.version>1.47.0</playwright.version>
        <junit.version>5.11.3</junit.version>
        <surefire.version>3.5.2</surefire.version>
        <jacoco.version>0.8.12</jacoco.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>com.microsoft.playwright</groupId>
            <artifactId>playwright</artifactId>
            <version>${playwright.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${surefire.version}</version>
                <configuration>
                    <!--
                      Run sequentially. The shared Playwright/Browser instance and its
                      driver connection are not thread-safe, so tests must not run in
                      parallel against the same browser. Isolation between tests is
                      provided by a fresh BrowserContext per test (see BaseTest).
                    -->
                    <forkCount>1</forkCount>
                    <reuseForks>true</reuseForks>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
                <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${jacoco.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <!--
                      Attach the JaCoCo agent before tests run so coverage is
                      recorded into target/jacoco.exec, then render an HTML/XML
                      report during the verify phase.
                    -->
                    <execution>
                        <id>prepare-agent</id>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>prepare-agent</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>report</id>
                        <phase>verify</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>report</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

# saucedemo-ui-playwright

End-to-end UI automation for **Swag Labs** (https://www.saucedemo.com/) built with
**Java 21 + Playwright + JUnit 5**, following the Page Object Model (POM) with a
`BasePage` interaction-wrapper abstraction for consistent, low-flakiness waits.

> Framework: **Playwright Standalone** (pure Playwright — no Cucumber/Gherkin).

## Tech stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Language | Java 21 |
| Browser automation | Playwright for Java |
| Test runner | JUnit 5 (Jupiter) |
| Build | Maven |

## Project structure

```
src/test/java/com/saucedemo/
├── base/
│   ├── BasePage.java          # Wait-then-act wrapper (click/type/getText/visibility)
│   └── BaseTest.java          # Playwright/browser/context lifecycle + login helpers
├── config/
│   ├── TestConfig.java        # Loads config.properties (overridable via -D)
│   └── TestData.java          # Product names & expected messages
├── pages/
│   ├── LoginPage.java
│   ├── InventoryPage.java
│   ├── ProductDetailPage.java
│   ├── CartPage.java
│   ├── CheckoutInformationPage.java
│   ├── CheckoutOverviewPage.java
│   ├── CheckoutCompletePage.java
│   └── components/HeaderComponent.java   # Shared cart badge + burger menu
└── tests/
    ├── AuthenticationTest.java   # TC-AUTH-001..009
    ├── InventoryTest.java        # TC-INV-001..006
    ├── CartTest.java             # TC-CART-001..006
    ├── CheckoutTest.java         # TC-CHK-001..008
    └── NavigationTest.java       # TC-NAV-001..002
```

## Design: Page Object Model + BasePage

Page Objects contain **only locators and business flows**. All UI interactions go
through `BasePage`, which waits for the element to reach the correct state before
acting (e.g. `click` waits for visibility, `type` waits then fills). This keeps
explicit waits consistent everywhere and avoids duplication.

`BaseTest` shares one browser per test class but gives **each test a fresh
`BrowserContext`**, so session and cart state never leak between tests.

## Running the tests

```bash
# Install browsers once (downloads the Playwright browser binaries)
mvn compile
mvn exec:java -e -Dexec.mainClass=com.microsoft.playwright.CLI -Dexec.args="install"

# Run the full suite (headless by default)
mvn test

# Run headed / with a specific browser
mvn test -Dheadless=false -Dbrowser=chromium

# Run a single feature
mvn test -Dtest=CheckoutTest
```

### Configuration

Defaults live in `src/test/resources/config.properties` and can be overridden at
runtime with `-D` flags: `base.url`, `browser` (`chromium`/`firefox`/`webkit`),
`headless`, `timeout`.

## Coverage

31 tests across 5 features — Authentication (9), Inventory (6), Cart (6),
Checkout (8), Navigation (2) — mapped 1:1 to the cases in `docs/test-cases.md`.

### Notes on real app behaviour

A couple of test cases document expectations the live saucedemo app does not
actually honour; the tests assert the **real** behaviour and call this out:

- **TC-INV-006** — the sort selection is *not* persisted across the product
  detail round trip; it resets to the default Name (A→Z).
- **TC-NAV-002** — *Reset App State* clears the cart badge immediately but only
  relabels the inventory buttons after a page reload.

> not as product coverage.
